review.source: review.md (owner follow-up code review at the repository root; kept untracked and git-ignored so the checkout stays clean, bytes unchanged)
resolved_parts: Intermediate-issued client chains are rejected with typed ErrUntrusted (round one).
CRL membership is matched by issuer and serial, never by serial alone (round one).
Regression coverage exists for intermediate-chain denial and cross-issuer serial collision (round one).
review.summary: The round-two follow-up review confirmed both round-one fixes accept only a single CRL and found the remaining security gap: the guard configured anchors of a second issuer but accepted that issuer's client certificates while certifying only one CRL, so revocations issued by the uncovered issuer could never be enforced. Smallest suitable fix chosen: reject every client leaf whose issuer is not the anchor that signed the configured CRL, keep issuer-plus-serial matching, and assert the contract in the rewritten cross-issuer regression.

security_review.credentials: Certificates carry synthetic test-only keys and are committed as clearly marked fixture data; the guard never emits or persists private key material beyond the operator-configured listener pair; scope maps are copied defensively at construction and per verdict
security_review.authority: Terminal certificate of each verified chain must be a configured anchor and the chain must be exactly [leaf, anchor] with the leaf issued directly by that anchor, so intermediate CAs cannot authenticate while the single revocation authority is an anchor; leaf validity is judged at the authoritative clock, the CRL must be signature-verified, structurally valid and fresh before membership, and every chain certificate the CRL issuer itself issued must carry a serial absent from the CRL (issuer, serial matching per RFC 5280, never serial alone); verdicts precede decode and scope enforcement before any ingest side effect
security_review.storage: No parallel storage authority; the guard imports only the standard library and internal/contracts and the unchanged C05 adapter remains the single durability boundary
security_review.transport: TLS 1.3 only, RequireAndVerifyClientCert, local anchors as the only ClientCAs pool, session tickets disabled and VerifyConnection wired to the same authoritative verdict on every connection including resumes; revocation is a locally delivered signed CRL rechecked against the clock on every verdict with fail-closed staleness; focused trace shows loopback-only connect() syscalls
security_review.dependencies: Standard library only; locked dependencies, Go toolchain pin and protected files unchanged

failed_attempts.phase: First guard version required HandshakeComplete in Verify
failed_attempts.note: TLS 1.3 invokes the server-side VerifyConnection after processing the client certificate, before the handshake completes, so the verdict never saw HandshakeComplete=true. Resolution: the verdict is keyed on the presented certificates and trust state; recorded in the committed implementation comments. No log was captured because this failure occurred during interactive development before evidence collection.
failed_attempts.resolution: Verify now accepts VerifyConnection handshake states; the tests pass with the committed implementation.

failed_attempts.phase: Negative dial assertions expected client-side handshake failure
failed_attempts.note: In TLS 1.3 the client handshake finishes before the server examines the client certificate, so a later server-side rejection cannot fail the dial. Resolution: the negative tests treat the listener verdict plus unchanged durable state as the authority. No log was captured; the committed tests encode this semantics.
failed_attempts.resolution: Tests now await listener-side typed failures with zero receipts and an unchanged manifest.

failed_attempts.phase: Discovery guard run against a C09-only partial test stream
failed_attempts.note: The guard intentionally requires a complete go test -json ./... stream; a C09-only run cannot satisfy it. Full-stream verification passed.
failed_attempts.resolution: Rerun the guard against the complete engine-tests.jsonl stream; no product change required.

failed_attempts.phase: Owner review found issuer-blind CRL revocation matching in the delivered guard
failed_attempts.note: The review is a valid must-find: serial-only membership allowed chains x509 verifies to authenticate revocations the guard can never load (intermediate CRLs) and could falsely reject a legitimate same-serial certificate from another configured anchor. Both reviewer regressions were reproduced against the pre-fix matcher by temporarily reverting internal/pki/identity.go in the worktree only; identity.go was then restored and the whole battery re-ran green against the fix.
failed_attempts.resolution: Committed the reviewer's smallest suitable option plus issuer-keyed membership: Verify rejects chains that are not [leaf, terminal anchor] (leaf issued directly by the configured anchor, documented restriction), CRL membership is matched on (issuer, serial) per RFC 5280, and two new regressions (intermediate-issued chain denied with typed ErrUntrusted; secondary-issued same-serial collector accepted while the primary-issued same serial stays revoked) bind the fix to the finding.

failed_attempts.phase: Owner follow-up review found issuers accepted without revocation coverage
failed_attempts.note: Valid must-fix: the guard accepts multiple configured anchors but certifies exactly one CRL, so secondary-issued collectors authenticated while their revocation could never be represented. The first red ran the new contract regression against the committed pre-fix source and the uncovered colliding collector authenticated and ingested (identities=2 receipts=2 failures=[]); the reverted-matcher experiment then reproduced both contract-bearing tests failing against the old code before identity.go was restored.
failed_attempts.resolution: New stores the fingerprint of the anchor that verified the CRL and Verify rejects [leaf, anchor] chains whose terminal anchor is not that CRL authority with typed ErrUntrusted (single-CRL coverage: only the CRL issuer population authenticates); the cross-issuer regression now asserts the secondary-issued same-serial collector is denied typed ErrUntrusted (never ErrRevoked), the covered primary-issued collector still ingests, and the primary-issued same serial stays revoked; the CA2 transcript capture in the typed-verdicts test was rebuilt to observe the typed denial because the old capture relied on the removed acceptance.

observed_limitations: Remote GitHub Actions execution unverified; no push/publication.
Local identity guard only: no HTTP/UI ingest endpoint, certificate issuance, OCSP or owner/tenant model; the real ingest endpoint belongs to C16 and rotation to C24.
Revocation depends on a trusted local clock and a locally delivered CRL; hostile host-clock rollback and network revocation transports are outside this scope.

The guard honors its documented single revocation authority: the accepted client-issuer set is exactly the configured anchor that signed the CRL (issuer-keyed, fail closed), so revocation coverage of a second issuer requires loading that issuer's own CRL, which the single-RevocationListPEM option cannot carry today and C24 owns rotation/multi-authority work.
Loopback tracing of the focused mTLS binary does not certify C13 decoy isolation, physical power-loss recovery or the full domain workflow.
No C30 usability or C40 release claim.
rollback_or_recovery_observation: The guard is process-local state with no durable writes: redeploying a stale or invalid configuration fails closed at construction and cannot poison storage. Already-ingested events and prior receipts stay valid under the unchanged C05 authority; a later revocation is enforced by configuration-only change on the next connection.

verification_notes: Validation ran against the review-fix mTLS source, fixtures, guards and documentation; the delivered guard c89127f8f7c20e0b1f65cabcfbc96185a009845c stayed exercised in the same battery plus the review-driven regressions. The diff check and clean-clone runs used isolated temporary candidate snapshots: no branch, remote ref or delivery commit moved during candidate verification. TLS 1.3 invokes the server-side VerifyConnection between client-certificate processing and handshake completion, so typed verdicts are evaluated on captured real ConnectionState values while transport denials are asserted from the listener outcome, receipts and unchanged manifest. Existing C07 event bytes are reused unchanged through the real sensor/store pipeline. The review fix republished narrative counts and hashes for this revision (146 Go events, 22 anchors, 14 loopback connects). Review round one pre-fix code is c89127f8f7c20e0b1f65cabcfbc96185a009845c and its fix is d1eebc79bc24455b6f1907e3b343c8effc255800; review round two proved the uncovered-issuer gap (secondary-issued collector accepted and ingested under the old matcher in docs/evidence/C09/review-red-uncovered-issuer.log), fixed it as CRL-issuer-coverage rejection keyed on the CRL-signing anchor fingerprint, rebuilt the CA2 transcript-capture section of the typed-verdicts test to its typed denial, and re-certified the whole battery plus the clean clone of the candidate snapshot. clean_snapshot records the separate temporary source-proof object; metadata edits made after candidate verification only publish these evidence fields, matching the recorded C09 delivery precedent, and the post-commit re-verification re-ran the validators, focused tests and a clean clone of the real fix commit.
